post_title: What will the National Bank of Poland's EUR/PLN reference rate be on 13 November 2026?

question.title: What will the National Bank of Poland's EUR/PLN reference rate be on 13 November 2026?
question.description:
The National Bank of Poland (NBP) publishes Table A of exchange rates — mid ("średnie") rates of foreign currencies in zloty — for every business day, with the table normally appearing between 11:45 and 12:15 CET. The EUR mid rate is Poland's headline reference rate for accounting, tax and contractual purposes, and the daily EUR/PLN fixing is the most closely watched gauge of the zloty.

Status quo as of 30 October 2026: the zloty is close to its weakest level in about three years. NBP's EUR mid rate rose from a 2026 low of roughly 4.20 in late January to 4.4090 on 28 October — its highest level in over a year — before easing to 4.3951 on 29 October and 4.3955 on 30 October. Recent daily Table A EUR values: 23 Oct 4.3917; 26 Oct 4.4026; 27 Oct 4.4056; 28 Oct 4.4090; 29 Oct 4.3951; 30 Oct 4.3955. Daily moves of 0.1–0.5% have been routine, and the pair broke above 4.40 repeatedly in late October.

Monetary policy: NBP's reference rate has been 3.75% since the March 2026 cut and was held at the September and October 2026 Monetary Policy Council meetings, with CPI inflation running around 3.4% y/y in August and 4.0% y/y in September 2026 — above the 2.5% target, which limits room for rate cuts. The Council meets next on 3–4 November 2026 (before the 13 November fixing) and 1–2 December 2026.

Politics and institutions: on 9 October 2026 the Sejm's Constitutional Accountability Committee voted to recommend that NBP Governor Adam Glapiński face the State Tribunal on eight charges; the full Sejm vote is planned for its 17–19 November sitting, i.e. a few days after the 13 November fixing. There is also uncertainty about the composition of NBP's management board. Economists (for instance Commerzbank and DM BOŚ commentary in late October 2026) attribute the zloty's underperformance versus other central European currencies mainly to this Poland-specific institutional uncertainty combined with a rise in global risk aversion.

Direction is genuinely contested: forwards and many bank research forecasts imply some zloty recovery (one aggregator of bank projections points to roughly 4.30 by December 2026), while political risk and the approach of the Sejm vote argue for continued weakness.

The reporting date: 13 November 2026 is an ordinary Polish business day, and only that day's fixing determines the answer — 11 November is Independence Day, a public holiday on which no Table A is published, and the 12 November fixing plays no part in resolution. No NBP rate decision or other Polish monetary-policy event falls on 13 November, so the outcome will be driven by market positioning and global risk sentiment rather than by a scheduled announcement.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the euro (EUR) mid rate reported in the National Bank of Poland's Table A of exchange rates ("kursy średnie") for 13 November 2026, expressed in Polish zloty per 1 euro. The value is the EUR entry in the Table A row dated 2026-11-13, read from NBP's Table A page (https://nbp.pl/statystyka-i-sprawozdawczosc/kursy/tabela-a) or, if that page has since rolled over to a later table, from NBP's 2026 Table A archive file (https://static.nbp.pl/dane/kursy/Archiwum/archiwum_tab_a_2026.xls). For example, if the 13 November 2026 table lists EUR at 4.3955, the question resolves as 4.3955. If NBP publishes no Table A with a 2026-11-13 date, the most recent Table A published on or before 13 November 2026 is used instead.
